title: Customer network commissioning field notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a field-oriented commissioning guide and sticky-notes collection for customer network installs where we hand off the initial Redwood Private control plane and inference nodes into a customer-managed network. Unlike the formal playbook, these are pragmatic scripts, terraform gotchas, and quick rollback ideas that we discovered during the last three pilots. Keep informal — intended for solutions engineers + SREs doing the first two installs.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target: single-region on-prem or colo with 3 availability racks (compute, control, storage).
- Customer provides L2/L3 connectivity between Redwood management plane subnet(s) and tenant inference subnet(s).
- We expect a customer firewall/NAT and optional outbound-proxy for updates; air-gapped installs may use an allowed-update-bucket flow.
- This doc focuses on network commissioning and terraform iteration notes; infra provisioning steps are in separate runbooks.

High-level flow (field sequence):
1) Pre-kickoff checklist (day -3 to -1):
   - Confirm IP plan: management /24, inference /22, storage /24, jumpbox /28. Get CIDR ranges in writing.
   - Verify BGP peering requirements (if any) and MTU (8250 for racks supporting RDMA).
   - Validate A-records and internal DNS zone: controlplane.redwood.local + bootstrap hostnames.
   - Get customer ACL template and list of required outbound domains (S3, package repos).
   - Share SSH pubkey for jumpbox and ensure KMS/HSM info for key wrapping if customer requires.

2) Day 0: onsite/remote handoff and initial connectivity tests:
   - From customer jumpbox: ping controlplane VIP, curl health endpoint (HTTP 200 expected) on 9443.
   - Netcat checks for ports: 22, 443, 50051 (gRPC), 2049/NFS if storage is customer-managed.
   - Check path MTU and TCP MSS; if fragmentation seen, plan for lowering MSS in iptables masquerade rules.

3) Terraform pattern we used (field note):
   - Use module instance per rack to avoid drift during partial upgrades. Example (pseudo):
     module "rack_a_network" {
       source = "github.com/redwood-inference/tf-modules//network/rack"
       cidr_block = "10.40.0.0/22"
       vlan_id = 120
       bgp_asn = 65010
     }
   - DO NOT change module variable names between minor TF upgrades — we've seen state mismatch where resource IDs are re-created. If you must rename variables, include a migration mapping in the PR.
   - For air-gapped customers, wrap provider blocks with "skip_remote_checks = true" pattern and maintain a local mirror URL list.

Terraform quirks observed in pilots:
- aws_vpc/vlan-like modules on vendor X switches returned unpredictable resource IDs when VLAN tag changes were applied out of band. Workaround: run a read-only plan after any manual switch change to surface diffs before apply.
- Provider plugin version pins are critical: loosened pins caused implicit resource recreation. Always include a provider_version.tf alongside the module.
- State locking: for on-prem installs that use an internal S3-compatible object store, we saw eventual consistency issues when multiple engineers ran apply in quick succession. Use a short (30s) retry with exponential backoff and prefer Dynamo-style locks if available.

Network commissioning checklist (operator-friendly):
- [ ] Confirm routing adjacency between customer router and Redwood control plane VLAN.
- [ ] Verify ACLs allow outbound to hosting registry and artifact mirror IPs.
- [ ] Confirm NTP from customer time servers (critical for cert validation).
- [ ] Ensure MTU is consistent across TOR-switch -> NIC; set jumbo frames only if entire path supports it.
- [ ] Validate DNS search domains include redwood internal zone.
- [ ] Confirm customer agrees to prefix-level logging on border firewall for first 72 hours.

Upgrade and rollback strategy (network-focused):
- Upgrade window: schedule a maintenance window with customer and enable maintenance routes (BGP community to prefer old control plane) to divert traffic in case of failure.
- Canary plan: bring up new control-plane nodes in parallel on an isolated management VLAN, run smoke tests (auth, model load) then flip routes over.
- Quick rollback: keep previous control-plane images and terraform state snapshot. To rollback routes, revert BGP community announcement and re-run terraform apply using the saved state snapshot.
- Database migration: treat DB schema changes as separate change windows. If a network upgrade touches DB connectivity, prefer rolling upgrades with connection draining.

Troubleshooting notes (rapid remedies):
- Symptom: nodes unable to pull images behind an outbound proxy. Quick check: curl -I --proxy http://<proxy> <mirror>/manifest.json. If TLS error, check proxy TLS interception certs and add CA to node truststore.
- Symptom: intermittent gRPC disconnects at 80k tokens/s. Quick check: run iperf3 between inference node and control plane to rule out packet loss. If high packet drops, inspect switch counters for link flaps and check NIC firmware.
- Symptom: weird terraform plan that wants to recreate a public IP for control VIP. Quick remedy: look for subtle tag differences or provider version drift; import the resource with terraform import and reconcile state instead of apply.

Security and compliance reminders:
- Avoid storing customer secrets in plain tfvars in the repo. Use vault-sealed variables and reference via external data source at apply time.
- KMS/HSM integration: ensure key rotation schedule and reachable KMS endpoints are documented with customer SecOps.

Open questions surfaced from pilots (to resolve in formal playbook):
- Should we standardize on a single CIDR sizing template (e.g., management /24, nodes /22) or allow flexible sizing? Pros/cons and bill impact for tiny customers.
- How to better automate verification of ACLs from customer-managed firewalls without asking them to run manual test scripts? Could we provide a short containerized test harness?
- When to insist customers provide BGP vs static routes (security vs operational familiarity)?

Action items (short-term):
- Marco: draft a tiny containerized network-test image that runs DNS, port, and MTU checks and uploads results to a pre-signed URL. (owner: Marco, due: 2025-03-19)
- Anika: add provider_version.tf template and a migration checklist to the tf-modules repo. (owner: Anika, due: 2025-03-17)
- Priya: consolidate the last three pilots' IP plans into a short reference table for Solutions Engineers. (owner: Priya, due: 2025-03-20)

Appendix A — quick command snippets (for jumpbox):
- curl health: curl -k https://controlplane.internal:9443/healthz
- netcat port test: nc -vz controlplane.internal 50051
- check MTU path: sudo ip route get 10.40.1.3; sudo ping -M do -s 1472 controlplane.internal
- terraform import example: terraform import module.rack_a_network.vlan_resource vlan-12345

Appendix B — artifacts and diagrams:
- Refer to linked_artifacts above for the PR with provider version template and a rough diagram. Attach a hand-drawn rack sketch in final playbook.

Notes to self: we should fold any durable items from this doc into the canonical onboarding playbook, but keep the commissioning checklist as a small laminated card for field engineers. Remember to capture customer feedback about running maintenance during business hours vs. after hours — got pushback from RetailPilot-2.

End of notes.
